source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1.First, make sure you have a CIFS share available and that you already know the share's IP address, path, username, and password.
2.Login bmc WebUI
3.mkdir /mnt/cifs_mount
4.mount -t cifs //共享IP地址/共享路徑 /mnt/cifs_mount -o
CIFS — //<IP to connect for CIFS file system>/<file path>/<image name>
username=your_username,password=your_password
NOTE:Please replace share IP address, share path, your_username and your_password with the actual information of your CIFS share.
5. Use df -h confirm whether the mount is successful
6. Image mount using OpenBMC's Web GUI. From the remote console interface, select Media -> Activate, then select Media -> Mount virtual media.
7. In the "Mount Media File from Network" option, enter your CIFS share path, for example: //myserver.mycompany.com/media/myCD.ISO.
8. From the "Local Media Mounted" section, select your software format (probably CD/DVD), then click "Browse" to find the software file, click "Open", then click "Mount".
9.Once it's done, you can go into the mounted ISO and do things like install an operating system.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: CIFS share/URL with a reachable CIFS image + BMC web + OS block tools
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Mount image via CIFS: mount the install image via CIFS from the BMC web -> Media -> Mount Virtual Media (CIFS share/URL: ${VM_SHARE:?operator must set the virtual media share or server url}/${VM_PATH:?operator must set the path on the share}/${VM_IMAGE:?operator must set the image file name}), then confirm the image appears as a boot/block device sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lsblk 2>&1; dmesg | tail -n 15 2>&1"; state-changing mount.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the OS block-device list + BMC web mount status so the user confirms the CIFS image mounted cleanly and is accessible.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: mounting an image shares it to the host and can autostart the OS; use a user-designated image URL and unmount after.

original_test_intent: Validate CIFS-backed BMC virtual media, remote-console connectivity and host CD-ROM exposure; the source also mentions an auto-install program but does not define whether installation is required.
original_method: Prepare and locally mount a CIFS share, log into BMC WebUI, activate and mount the image through remote console, then inspect host visibility and potentially enter an installer.
manual_activity: If corrected as a mount-only WebUI case, an engineer operates and observes the BMC remote-console controls; any boot/install action requires a separate explicit destructive plan.
required_inputs: Exact CIFS server/share/path/image/hash and security mode
Isolated SUT and protected disk inventory
BMC virtual-media SOP and expected device identity
safety_requirements: Do not execute the malformed mount line or place credentials in command arguments/logs.
Do not boot, auto-install, repartition or write storage without explicit target-disk approval.
Baseline block devices/boot order and use read-only media where supported.
Deactivate/unmount after evidence; stop on unexpected installer/boot/device state and never retry automatically.
agent_execution_scope: After correction, validate image metadata, collect read-only device/log evidence and analyze operator-provided WebUI/console artifacts.
Do not operate the manual WebUI, start installation or assign the verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve intended end state and corrected CIFS contract.
Operate WebUI/console for the approved scope and decide the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its generic VM_SHARE path and `lsblk` check do not repair the broken CIFS command, prove remote-console success, distinguish mount from install or protect disks; sshpass/host-key bypass is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No action until the source scope is corrected. For mount-only coverage, use the vendor WebUI/SOP, protected secrets, immutable image hash, read-only device inventory and explicit deactivation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All malformed CIFS text, WebUI sequence, auto-install wording and 15/5-minute values remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Split reversible CIFS virtual-media mount/visibility from any boot or automated installation. Define each target, evidence, cleanup and recovery independently.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: BMC with documented CIFS virtual-media support.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor virtual-media and CIFS security documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes implicit transition from mount to installer and adds disk protection/cleanup; original remains preserved.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Makes mount coverage testable without falsely claiming installation coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Owner scope decision and corrected share contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Bootable media can alter boot flow and overwrite storage.

project_override_considerations: A project may authorize only mount/visibility and record that narrower plan as complete for that project; it must not claim the source's undefined auto-install result. Any install belongs in an explicit disk-targeted plan.
expected_evidence: Pre/post host device inventory and exact CD-ROM identity

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure contains an incomplete CIFS command and moves from virtual-media mounting to possible OS installation; Criteria have missing numbering and require an auto-install program without specifying an install target or expected state.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Mount-only and destructive installation are materially different tests with different safety boundaries. Executing before the owner selects one can expose or overwrite host storage, so this is a genuine semantic/safety block.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its generic partial flow as insufficient for the corrupted source and installer risk.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on BLOCKED and sharpens the split between reversible mount, boot and install.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: BLOCKED rests on irreducible scope ambiguity, not merely missing share/image parameters or WebUI attendance.

review_improvement: Defines the exact semantic decision required before safe execution and preserves disk/cleanup boundaries.
independent_technical_reasoning: A virtual-media mount is reversible, but an auto-installer can overwrite disks. Because the source treats these as one acceptance path without identifying a target or authorization, automation or manual execution cannot safely infer the intended end state.
